https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqlw.text: Image source, DHS Image caption, The Department of Homeland Security released a mugshot of Yiannopoulos By George Wright Published 29 August 2026, 18:25 BST Updated 2 hours ago British right-wing political commentator Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the United States after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Yiannopoulos, 41, a former editor of Breitbart News and one time political aide to rapper Kanye West, was deported on Friday, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Yiannopoulos, "an illegal alien from the United Kingdom" had been sent "back to his home country", a DHS spokesperson said in a statement given to the BBC. The self-styled provocateur has called himself the "most fabulous supervillain on the internet" and advocated for stricter US immigration controls. His critics call him a purveyor of hate speech. Yiannopoulos, who grew up in Kent in the south of England, was arrested on 27 August after arriving at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport. He flew into the US in May 2019 and "chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation's laws", the DHS said. He has previously cheered on ICE raids, last year calling for "total legal immunity for ICE agents when they're on duty". He wrote on social media in 2025: "We have got to deport millions and millions of people. Without that, nothing else matters." Yiannopoulos also advocated "on the spot deportation for anyone who can't prove they are in the US legally" on social media. Yiannopoulos was an early supporter of Donald Trump during the 2016 election, headlining an event that year called Gays for Trump during the Republican National Convention. The commentator has since become a critic of the US president, but still voices support for his agenda. He wrote on X in March this year that Trump had "lost his way, bought off by foreign interests". Yiannopoulos has courted controversy with his comments on transgender people, Muslims, Black Lives Matter, feminists and gay people, even though he himself identified as gay. He now calls himself an "ex-gay". In 2020, he assisted West in the rapper's unsuccessful bid to become president. He also worked for Marjorie Taylor Greene, a former Republican congresswoman who fell out with Trump and became a fierce critic before resigning from office. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The commentator has become a critic of Donald Trump, but still voices support for his agenda Laura Loomer, a far-right commentator and Trump ally who has feuded with Yiannopoulos, took credit for his arrest by ICE, claiming on X on Friday night that his flight back to the UK had already departed. "This subversive foreign agent is already out of the United States and DHS tells me he's NEVER allowed to come back to the United States ever again," she wrote. In 2017, he was disinvited from speaking at CPAC, a US conservative conference that also hosted Trump, after footage emerged of Yiannopoulos appearing to condone paedophilia. He also later apologised and resigned from Breitbart. He denied the allegations and said he had been speaking about his own experiences as a child. Yiannopoulos was once regularly linked with the alt-right, a disparate group that is outspoken against political correctness and feminism, and which includes neo-Nazis and white supremacists among its ranks. He has said he did not consider himself part of the alt-right, although he has called it "energising and exciting". The BBC has approached the Home Office for comment. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/14/a-xi.text: Menü Kereső A XIII. kerület nem támogatja, hogy a melegek méltóságáról szóló mondat szerepeljen Nádasdy Ádám emléktábláján Belföld Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A XIII. kerületi önkormányzat általánosságban nem támogatja, hogy az általa állított emléktáblákon származásra, nemi identitásra vagy vallási hovatartozásra utaló szöveg szerepeljen. Ezzel indokolták a Telex kérdésére, hogy miért hagynák le Nádasdy Ádám emléktáblájáról a melegek méltóságáról szóló részt. Nádasdy Ádám költő, nyelvész, műfordító március 29-én, 79 éves korában halt meg . Újlipótváros önkormányzata jövő februárban emléktáblát szeretne állítani Nádasdy 80. születésnapja alkalmából. A táblát azon a házon helyeznék el, ahol Nádasdy évtizedek óta élt. A tervről nyáron levelet küldtek a nyelvész özvegyének és családjának, és kikérték a véleményüket, hogy mi szerepeljen az emléktáblán. „Mindent intéznek, a költségeket vállalják, a ház lakóival is egyeztetnek. A család csak mondja meg, milyen szöveget szeretne, és ki legyen az avatáson a szónok” – írta Facebook-oldalán Török András művelődéstörténész, akit Nádasdy családja bevont az emléktábláról szóló ötletelésbe. „Az nem volt kérdés, hogy Ádám négy tételes önmeghtatározása, Tanár, Nyelvész, Költő, Műfordító és az évszámok szerepeljenek […] De felmerült, hogy a meleg társadalomra tett hatására szerepeljen valami utalás. Hiszen ezt nem lehetett odaírni ötödik foglalkozásnak, hiszen a legkevésbé sem volt »meleg aktivista«” – írta Török, és megosztotta az önkormányzatnak elküldött javaslatot, amin az szerepelt, hogy: „Aki sokat tett a magyar melegek méltóságáért.” A kerület azonban nem támogatta ezt a javaslatot, és egy olyan változatot küldtek vissza, amin már nem szerepelt ez a sor. „Döbbenetünkre néhány hét múlva egy másik változat jött vissza a polgármester tanácsadójától, aki eddig is az ügyet intézte. Azt fűzte hozzá, hogy azt a változatot tudják a lakók elé tárni” – tette hozzá Török. A Telex megkeresésére a XIII. kerület önkormányzata kifejtette, hogy miért nem támogatják az eredeti változatot. Azt írták: „Önkormányzatunk általánosságban nem támogatja, hogy az általa állított emléktáblákon a személy származására, nemi identitására vagy vallási hovatartozására utaló szöveg jelenjen meg. A konkrét ügyben egy munkaközi anyagban is ennek az elvnek a szellemében született a javaslatunk. Ezt cenzúrának hívni igaztalan túlzás. Sajnálatosnak tartjuk, hogy egy, az egyeztetésben közvetlenül részt sem vevő személy erről a magánvéleményét a nyilvánosság elé tárta.” Hozzátették: „Önkormányzatunk a kialakult helyzetre való tekintettel Nádasdy Ádám családjának kezdeményezésére az elkövetkezendő időszakban közösen és egyetértésben fogja keresni a róla való méltó megemlékezés lehetőségét.” Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/29/t.text: TMT Newswire GlobeNewswire Silentbox Takes Acoustic Booths into the Space-as-a-Service (SPaaS) Era By GlobeNewswire September 29, 2026 10 Resize Small Medium Large Acoustic booth manufacturer Silentbox is applying the Space-as-a-Service (SPaaS) model to coworking spaces and business centres. WARSAW, POLAND, Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Silentbox , a European manufacturer of acoustic booths, has announced an investment in Space-as-a-Service (SPaaS), turning its acoustic booths into bookable, pay-per-use spaces for calls, meetings and focused work in shared and public locations. The model is already operating commercially at a shopping centre in Lisbon, where Silentbox booths average 78% occupancy and more than 500 bookings per month, with a user rating of 4.8 out of 5. Under the SPaaS model, an acoustic booth is no longer permanently assigned to a single company or team. Instead, it becomes a shared, bookable resource that can be used throughout the day for calls, meetings, focused work or confidential conversations. Users book and pay for the booth when they need it, while coworking spaces, business centres and other location owners can generate additional revenue from existing floor space. Get the latest news delivered to your inbox Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy . Silentbox Cloud provides the digital infrastructure for booking, payment, access and workspace management. The platform supports the SPaaS model, enabling location owners to offer acoustic booths as bookable spaces without permanently allocating them to individual users or companies. Space-as-a-Service (SPaaS) Advertisement Space-as-a-Service brings the principle of paying for access rather than ownership to the workplace market. Instead of permanently allocating space to a single company or team, shared spaces can be made available to different users according to their needs. Silentbox applies this model to acoustic booths, turning a unit of workplace infrastructure into a shared, bookable resource. For shopping centres, airports, business centres, coworking spaces and offices, this creates an opportunity to offer additional bookable space without permanently allocating it to individual users - while generating additional revenue from existing floor space. European Market Position Founded in 2019, Silentbox is a European manufacturer of acoustic booths, with more than 500 acoustic booths installed across 30+ countries and 92 cities. Advertisement Silentbox designs and manufactures its booths in-house, combining patented designs with certified acoustic performance. Its Premium line has been laboratory-tested according to ISO 11957 and ISO 23351-1, with sound insulation of up to 35 dB, depending on the model and configuration. Investment and Expansion The investment marks Silentbox’s expansion from manufacturing acoustic infrastructure into Space-as-a-Service, creating a new business model around bookable acoustic booths. The company plans to expand its SPaaS network across European and international markets, targeting offices, shopping centres, airports, business centres and coworking spaces. "Space-as-a-Service changes how acoustic workspace can be accessed. Instead of being permanently assigned to one company or team, an acoustic booth can be made available to different users throughout the day. We see an opportunity to make acoustic infrastructure more flexible and accessible while giving location owners a new way to use their existing floor space.” - Svyatoslav Serbin, Co-Founder of Silentbox Advertisement About Silentbox Silentbox is a European manufacturer of acoustic booths founded in 2019. The company designs and manufactures acoustic workplace solutions for offices and public spaces, combining in-house production with its own product development and patented designs. Silentbox is now expanding beyond manufacturing into Space-as-a-Service, developing a model that combines acoustic booth infrastructure with digital booking, payment, access and workspace management through Silentbox Cloud. https://www.dw.com/en/us-california-wild.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OLpg Thousands have had to evacuate as the wildfire continued to spread Image: Jae C. Hong/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement At least six expensive properties have been engulfed by fast-spreading wildfires on the southern coast of California, prompting thousands of people to evacuate. The Orange County Fire Authority said on X that the so-called Norte fire had scorched about 465 acres (188 hectares) and that at least four homes had been impacted in the affluent San Juan Capistrano municipality. Black smoke billowing from the hills was visible for miles as firefighters tried to contain the fast-moving blaze. The agency said firefighters were "aggressively attacking the fire from ground and air" and repeatedly requested people to stay away from the area. Danger of fire spreading remains as thousands without power The Norte fire started in the coastal city of San Clemente and wind drove it into San Juan Capistrano. The National Weather Service warned of "high risk for large fires and rapid fire growth," especially over Los Angeles and Ventura counties, as well as the mountains and foothills of San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties The wildfires have continued to worsen due to the intense Santa Ana winds, low humidity and unseasonably high temperatures. According to forecasters, wind gusts of up to 50-70 miles (80-110 kilometers) per hour were recorded in the mountains, with coastal and valley areas seeing gusts between 35 and 55 miles per hour. Authorities have turned off the electricity supply to reduce the risk of electrical sparks that the heavy wind gusts could carry, leaving thousands of people in the state without power. Newsflash Newsroom , 18.10.2026, 13:55 PROTESTS – French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said that 1,200 people had been arrested after large-scale protests over declining public services and the cost of living turned violent in several parts of the country on Saturday. Lecornu said 150 police officers had been injured in clashes with demonstrators. Officially authorised marches were accompanied by groups of violent individuals who gathered in areas where demonstrations were banned in an attempt to provoke incidents. For those protesting across France, including in Paris, the demonstrations brought together a range of grievances. The protests began with students and were joined by civil servants, trade unions, left-wing political groups and members of the so-called Yellow Vest movement, who protested against the cost of living ten years ago, during President Macron’s first term, news agencies report. Several European countries were also affected by protests on Saturday over the deterioration of social services and living standards. In Portugal, tens of thousands of people took to the streets in Lisbon, mainly to protest against rents doubling between 2017 and the present day. In Italy, clashes broke out between demonstrators and security forces in Milan and Bologna. Similar incidents occurred in Albania, where police fired rubber bullets at protesters who have been taking to the streets for several days to protest against corruption and Prime Minister Edi Rama. NATIONAL BUDGET – Romania’s 2027 budget must be built on realistic revenues, clear priorities and spending the state can afford, says interim Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare, who has been included in the cabinet proposed by Luca Niculescu. However, achieving this objective, which will fall to the future government, depends on striking a balance between available resources and meeting social demands, such as the indexation of pensions. Alexandru Nazare added that Romania had not yet reached a stage of economic recovery free from constraints, and that maintaining budgetary discipline was essential to avoid further imbalances. In his view, there were favourable conditions, given that the budget deficit for the first nine months of this year stood at just 3.82% of GDP, 1.5% lower than in the same period in 2025. Meanwhile, public administration debt continued to rise, reaching 1,205 billion lei (around 225 billion euros) in July. As a percentage of GDP, government debt has now edged above 60%, according to the National Institute of Statistics. Social pressure over issues such as pension indexation is nevertheless evident. Although annual indexation is required by law, it has been suspended over the past two years. The average pension in Romania does not exceed 3,000 lei (around 560 euros), while more than two million pensioners receive less than 2,500 lei. GOVERNMENT – In Bucharest, parliamentary committee hearings begin on Monday for the ministers proposed to join the team of prime minister-designate Luca Niculescu, ahead of the investiture vote scheduled to take place in plenary session on Tuesday afternoon. To be approved, the new government, made up of Social Democrats and independents, needs at least 233 votes in favour. Parliamentary support is expected to come from the Social Democratic Party (PSD), the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR), the national minorities and the United for Romania group. On Saturday, National Liberal Party (PNL) leader Ilie Bolojan announced that his party, which will move into opposition, would support the new government through a “conditional and case-by-case vote of necessity”, after signing an agreement with the prime minister-designate on Monday. The Save Romania Union (USR) and the Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR), meanwhile, will vote against the government. Luca Niculescu is the fourth nominee put forward by President Nicuşor Dan for the post of prime minister, following Parliament’s dismissal, through a motion of no confidence on 5 May, of the minority government formed by the PNL, USR and UDMR and led by Liberal Ilie Bolojan, who has been serving as caretaker prime minister ever since. ALERT – Lithuania asked residents to take shelter for around an hour this morning because of an unidentified flying object, the military and the National Crisis Management Centre said. During a red air alert, fighter jets serving with NATO’s air policing mission were scrambled and sent to the area, while Kaunas Airport, near Lithuania’s second-largest city, was closed, the centre said. Earlier, the Polish military said it was investigating a possible violation of the country’s airspace by an unidentified object. Latvia, Lithuania’s northern neighbour, also issued and subsequently lifted a yellow air alert in some areas along its border with Lithuania. Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered NATO airspace in the Baltic region in recent months. Kyiv has said they deviated from their intended flight paths because of Russian electronic jamming. The situation has heightened fears that Russia’s war against Ukraine could spread beyond NATO’s borders. On Saturday, Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two drones over the country’s territorial waters, days after two chemical product tankers were hit by drones near Romania’s Black Sea coast. These are the latest in a series of attacks highlighting the risks to commercial shipping on NATO’s eastern flank. Most of these incidents have taken place outside NATO members’ territorial waters. In the Republic of Moldova, on Romania’s north-eastern border, the authorities announced that another drone had crashed in a district in the north of the country, near the border with Ukraine. WEATHER – Predominantly overcast and cold weather is forecast today in northern, central, eastern and south-eastern Romania, where cloud cover will persist. Elsewhere, skies will be partly cloudy, with temperatures close to seasonal averages. There will be occasional rain in the eastern half of the country. In high mountain areas, particularly in the eastern Southern Carpathians, above 1,900 metres, precipitation will also fall as sleet and snow, with a fresh snow layer of more than 5 cm expected to accumulate. Over the past few hours, snowfall has continued to cause problems on the Transfăgărăşan mountain road, where a substantial layer of snow has built up. Snow has also fallen on Romania’s other high-altitude road, the Transalpina. In some mountain areas, the snow depth has reached 37 cm. Meteorologists say further snowfall is expected at high altitudes, but temperatures across the country will begin to rise from Tuesday. On Wednesday, temperatures in western and south-western Romania will reach 24 degrees Celsius. Today, maximum temperatures will range from 10 to 21 degrees Celsius. In Bucharest, temperatures will rise compared with the previous day, with a maximum of 17 to 18 degrees Celsius.
